EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows the hallmark para-disubstituted benzene out-of-plane C–H bending doublet in the 820–860 cm⁻¹ region (strong peaks at 824 and 853 cm⁻¹, with a companion at 843 cm⁻¹), consistent with a p-substituted phenyl. The presence of a distinct band near 640 cm⁻¹ supports a C–Cl vibration, favoring a chloro-substituted ring over the fluoro- or amino candidates. Aromatic and aliphatic C–H stretches are present (3075 and 3014 cm⁻¹ for aromatic; broad 2921 cm⁻¹ for aliphatic), consistent with a benzyl substituent (GFQ-003). The 1003 cm⁻¹ ring breathing and ~1025 cm⁻¹ C–O stretch fit a benzyl alcohol. p-Fluorobenzyl alcohol (3) would typically show a stronger C–F stretch near ~1100 cm⁻¹, which is absent, and amino-containing candidates should show NH stretches near 3300 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-002), which are not evident. Therefore, p-chlorobenzyl alcohol (OCc1ccc(Cl)cc1) best fits the observed Raman features.
